## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the condition wording under the hero temperature, the settings switch and its `shell.json` write-back, the code mappings (all 28 WMO and 48 wttr codes resolve to a condition, and every WMO code has wording), the empty input mask and the Bottom-layer placement all behave as described. Both new test scripts pass at this head (97 and 70 assertions), and the new wording tests fail against the base code as expected.

The wallpaper layer has four behavior issues, found by source review and small sandboxed probes. None of them affect the panel wording change.

### Rain leans against the wind

`Animation.js` intends a positive slant to mean travel to the right ("a westerly (270) sends rain to the right"), and the test asserts that sign. `FallingSheet` then applies it as `rotation: root.slant` and slides the sheet along its own +y axis. Qt's `Item.rotation` is clockwise, so local +y maps to `(-sin a, cos a)`, and a positive slant moves drops down and to the **left**.

```text
wind from 270 (westerly, blowing east)
  slantForWind(...)  -> +12.5 degrees   (intended: lean right)
  rotation: +12.5    -> drop travel x = -0.217 per unit fall  (moves left)
```

Values from a sandboxed probe of `Animation.js` with an Open-Meteo reading of code 63 and 20 km/h wind.

**Impact:** whenever Open-Meteo reports a bearing, precipitation drifts opposite to the real wind, which is the behavior the new `wind_direction_10m` request is meant to provide.

**Suggested change:** use `rotation: -root.slant` in `FallingSheet` (or invert `slantDirection` and its tests).

### With several monitors, the desktop alternates between panels' readings

Each bar surface has its own weather panel with its own fetches (refresh timer, opening the panel, middle-click). Every panel pushes its `resolvedCurrent` to the one shared service on change and every 20 s, and `applyWeather` simply overwrites `currentWeather`. The service's single `profile` drives every screen.

```text
panel A (screen 1): reading R1 ──push──┐        ┌──push──  ...every 20 s
panel B (screen 2): reading R2 ──push──┼─> service.currentWeather = last writer
                                       └─> all screens redraw with R1, R2, R1, ...
```

When the two readings differ (for example after one panel refreshes on open), every screen switches between them on each heartbeat until the other panel next refreshes (up to the 15-minute default). A different drop count makes `Repeater` clear and recreate all drops, which re-randomizes their positions. A different condition swaps renderers outright. This is traced from source and a sandboxed two-panel model. The on-screen effect was not observed in a live session.

**Impact:** visible periodic jumps on multi-monitor setups while readings diverge.

**Suggested change:** keep only the newest reading by observation time (Open-Meteo `current.time`, wttr `localObsDateTime`), or share one fetch between panels.

### "Session locked" never stops the layer

`Service.qml` looks up the lock with `shell.firstPartyServiceFor("omarchy.lock")`, which reads `_services`. `omarchy.lock` carries the `authentication` capability, and `ensureService` stores such services only in `AuthServiceStore`, never in `_services`. So `lockService` is always null and `lockActive` is always false. `Background.qml` already uses the same lookup at the base commit, so the pattern is inherited. This PR also lists the lock as a stop condition in the manual and in the setting description.

**Impact:** when the session is locked without the screensaver (for example a manual lock), the surfaces stay mapped and their animations keep running under the lock surface. The actual render cost in that state was not measured.

**Suggested change:** read a narrow lock-state flag exposed by the shell (fed from the isolated lock service), shared with `Background.qml`. Alternatively, drop the lock claim from the manual and the setting description.

### Conditions switch without the described cross-fade

The only fade is the 1200 ms `Behavior` on the layer's root opacity, which stays at 1 while `profile` is non-null. On a condition change, one renderer `Loader` deactivates and another activates in the same frame, so rain to snow is an instant cut. When the layer stops, `Service.qml` unmaps the surface immediately, so the fade-out is not visible either. Only the fade-in on map runs.

**Impact:** cosmetic. The PR description and the `WeatherAnimation.qml` header describe a cross-fade that does not happen.

**Suggested change:** keep the outgoing renderer until its own opacity reaches zero while the incoming one fades in. Alternatively, reword the description and comments.

### Smaller notes

**Renderers are built while the setting is off:** `pushAnimationState` runs on every `resolvedCurrent` change regardless of the setting. The service stores the reading, and the renderer `Loader`s bind only to `profile`, so each forecast result instantiates the renderer tree on every screen until the 70 s timeout frees it. Nothing animates or renders, but "pays nothing" does not quite hold. If the layer was mapped earlier in the session, full drop repeaters are built. Passing `profile: null` to the layer while disabled (and not previewing), or dropping the reading in `applyWeather` when disabled, avoids this.

**`preview` while the setting is off:** `active` requires `animationsEnabled`, so `omarchy-shell omarchy.weather-animation preview snow` answers `ok` and draws nothing by default. Either let a preview enable the layer temporarily (it already expires after ten minutes) or return a message saying animations are off.

**Optional test improvement:** the wiring block in `weather-animation-test.sh` matches source substrings. In sandboxed mutation runs, all 97 assertions still passed with the rotation sign flipped, the lock lookup replaced by `null`, and the opacity `Behavior` removed. An assertion that composes `slantForWind` with Qt's clockwise rotation would pin the rain direction.
